episodes.152784: Heavy rain brought flooding to parts of northeast Arkansas at the end of October.
episodes.153457: Tropical Storm Zeta passed quickly across the lower mid-Atlantic region on the morning of the 29th, but still brought 2-3 inches of rainfall to the foothills of the Blue Ridge and the Piedmont region.  Much of this rain fell within a 1-2 hour period, resulting in rapid flooding of several small streams.  Residual moisture in the wake of Zeta allowed for redevelopment of bands of slow-moving storms producing additional heavy rain, which also resulted in localized flooding across the Piedmont of Virginia.
episodes.153775: Tropical moisture streamed into the area as the remnants of Zeta approached and interacted with a stalled frontal boundary. A prolonged period of heavy rain led to flooding across portions of Northern Virginia.
episodes.153776: Tropical moisture streamed into the area as the remnants of Zeta approached and interacted with a stalled frontal boundary. A prolonged period of heavy rain led to flooding across portions of central and southern Maryland.
episodes.153824: An isolated waterspout was observed northwest of Boca Chica Key in association with rain showers developing along a weakening cold front boundary.
episodes.153835: Low pressure combined with the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Zeta tracking across the Middle Atlantic region produced heavy rain which caused flooding across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.

events.narrative: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Black River at Black Rock.

Western Branch at Upper Marlboro was in Minor Flood Stage during the indicated time period, reaching a peak level of 12.68 feet at 3:30 AM on October 30th. The Water Street bridge in Upper Marlboro was completely covered by water, and much of Race Track Road was flooded between Marlboro Pike and the community center.
Cedar Run at Aden was in Minor Flood stage during the indicated time period, reaching a peak level of 10.31 feet at 1:07 AM on October 30th. Fleetwood Road was flooded near Cedar Run.
Mattawoman Creek at Pomonkey was in Minor Flood stage during the indicated period. The peak level of 7.53 feet occurred at 9:45 AM October 30th. Pomfret Road was flooded.

Training thunderstorms formed along a boundary left in the wake of Tropical Storm Zeta, producing 2.5-4 inches of rain in a three to four hour period.  Rainfall rates were observed to be one to two inches per hour.  The Campbell County 911 Center reported that at least seven roads within the central part of the county were flooded and impassable.  This included Yellow Branch rising out of its banks near the intersection of Morman Mill Road and Patterson Road.
High water was reported on roadways between Linkwood and East New Market.

The St Mary's River at Great Mills was in Minor Flood stage during the indicated period. The peak level of 6.63 feet occurred at 9:00 AM on October 30th. Flat Iron Road was flooded, along with some yards in Great Mills.

events.narrative: A waterspout was observed by the contract weather observer and flight briefer at Naval Air Station Key West Boca Chica Field, about 8 miles north-northwest of the airfield.

The Roanoke River at Brookneal (BROV2) crested above moderate flood stage at 27.74 feet, which is about 35,100 cfs.  This is between a two and five year average return interval per USGS analysis for this gauge.  Typical impacts at this stage are that the nearby low-lying fields and woods are flooded, though the Brookneal Fish Hatchery pond furthest downstream may begin to experience some flooding.

Multiple personal weather stations in the upper Falling River basin indicated three to four inches of rain fell during the late evening hours of the 29th into the early morning hours of the 30th.  Runoff from this rain collected in the Falling River, with the gauge at the Falling River near Naruna (FLRV2) rising to 20.39 feet (10600 cfs).  This is between a 5- and 10-year average return interval for this river gauge per USGS stream statistics.
